text:
alex_ryan: Quick one — procurement looking at BatchOps (vendor demo last week). Their pricing has a 3-tier commit + burst model and an "embedded-ops" SKU that charges per embedding vector hour. Can someone sanity-check the numbers before I loop in procurement?

maria_g: I skimmed the quote. Two things jumped out: (1) 20% discount on committed vGPU hours but overage billed at 2x list, (2) embedding SKU is per-vector-hour, not per-request — weird.

kevin_sre: Can you paste the table they sent? small numbers/simple math will help.

alex_ryan: Pasting the clip from the PDF — sorry for the formatting:

```
Commit Tier A: 400 vGPU-hrs/mo @ $6/hr = $2400
Commit Tier B: 1200 vGPU-hrs/mo @ $5/hr = $6000
Burst buffer: +20% at same rate, overage billed at $12/hr
Embedding-ops SKU: $0.0009 per vector-hour (100M vectors/hr = $90k)
Support SLA: 99.5% for committed, 99.0% otherwise

Note: enterprise SSO + VPC add $1k/mo
```

lisa_finance: Whoa the embedding math is brutal if we stream batched metrics. We need an expected vector-hour forecast from the search team before committing. Jordan, can you add a row to the forecast?

jordan_pm: on it — I'll pull last quarter usage and project with the new feature. ETA EOD.

maria_g: Also ask BatchOps for a hard cap/overage negotiation. If they refuse, we need a way to auto-fallback to our cheaper hosted variant when burst > X%.

kevin_sre: Technical note: we should check whether their embedding vector-hours count includes cached KV reuse. If they count every call even when KV cached, cost can blow up. I'll ask for telemetry semantics.

alex_ryan: Good call. Also: does their SLA include model rollback / performance regression credits? The quote is silent. Procurement will want credits or at least rollback playbook.

lisa_finance: From a finance standpoint, propose these asks before renewal negotiation: 1) 30-day trial at Tier B pricing for one service, 2) explicit overage cap or tiered overage discounts, 3) invoice breakdown by SKU (vGPU, embedding, storage, network), 4) credit for SLA misses.

procurement_bot: Reminder: attach any vendor quotes to the procurement thread in Confluence and assign vendor-eval tag. Deadline for decision: 2024-06-15.

maria_g: I'm happy to draft the vendor questions. Alex, Kevin — what are your top 3 items we should push on?

kevin_sre: 1) Embedding vector-hour definition and caching behavior. 2) Hard overage cap and bursting policy. 3) Performance isolation guarantees for committed pools (cold start P95).

alex_ryan: I'll add: 4) Data residency + audit logs included or extra, 5) Rollback / pinned model versions support.

jordan_pm: I'll include an expected cost delta sheet in the forecast: current infra vs BatchOps (best-case/worst-case).

lisa_finance: If they won't give a reasonable overage cap, we should require a termination or price-protection clause for first 12 months.

alex_ryan: OK — plan: Maria will send vendor questions today, Kevin will ask the technical semantics, Jordan will update the forecast, Lisa will prepare finance asks. I'll coordinate and summarize for procurement. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

maria_g: Draft going out in 30m — ping me for edits.

kevin_sre: Posting a quick command I used to check vector emission counts in our telemetry in case they ask for examples:

```bash
# count emitted vectors per minute from the logs
grep "emit_vector" /var/log/service/*.log | cut -d\" \" -f4 | sort | uniq -c | tail -n 50
```

alex_ryan: Perfect. We'll attach the sample telemetry and the forecast to the procurement ticket.
